steps.observation: You have 60 seconds. What are three strategies for reducing carbon emissions in cities?

steps.action:
1. Electrify urban transportation  
   • Expand reliable public transit powered by renewable electricity (electric buses, light rail).  
   • Build dense networks of safe cycling and pedestrian infrastructure to shift short trips away from cars.  
   • Accelerate the uptake of electric cars, taxis and delivery fleets by installing fast-charge hubs and offering incentives.

2. Retrofit and decarbonize buildings  
   • Mandate high-efficiency standards for new construction (net-zero or passive-house codes).  
   • Launch large-scale programs to insulate existing buildings, replace gas boilers with electric heat pumps, and install smart energy management systems.  
   • Provide green financing and subsidies to homeowners and landlords to lower upfront costs.

3. Transition to clean, local energy sources  
   • Deploy rooftop and community solar, encourage battery storage, and use microgrids to supply neighborhoods with renewable power.  
   • Procure 100 % renewable electricity for municipal operations and create citywide renewable energy purchasing programs.  
   • Capture waste heat from industry, data centers and sewers to feed district heating networks, reducing reliance on fossil fuels.
